questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests mastery of advanced lock-free data structures, NUMA-aware memory placement, and cross-socket contention. It also probes practical design choices for zero-copy paths in high-throughput RPC.

## Key Concepts

- NUMA-aware memory placement and huge pages
- Lock-free queue with ABA avoidance via version counters
- Credit-based flow control and backpressure
- Memory ordering (acquire/release) and cache-line alignment
- Cross-socket latency benchmarking

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-code: enqueue
slot = (tail + 1) % N
if (credits[producer] > 0) {
  slots[slot].data = payload
  slots[slot].version = slots[slot].version + 1
  atomic_store(tail, slot, memory_order_release)
  atomic_fetch_add(&credits[producer], -1, memory_order_relaxed)
}
```

```javascript
// Pseudo-code: dequeue
slot = head
if (slots[slot].data != NULL) {
  payload = slots[slot].data
  slots[slot].data = NULL
  atomic_fetch_add(&head, 1, memory_order_release)
  atomic_fetch_add(&credits[consumer], 1, memory_order_relaxed)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you validate correctness under cacheline false sharing?
- How would you adapt the design for more than two NUMA nodes?

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates deep understanding of lock-free concurrent data structures, memory management, and NUMA-aware design in modern multicore systems. It tests practical knowledge of per-thread caching, safe memory reclamation, and performance optimization under contention.

## Key Concepts Tested

- **Lock-free algorithms**: Compare-and-swap loops, ABA prevention, memory ordering
- **Per-thread caches**: Fast path optimization, cache locality, false sharing avoidance
- **Hazard pointers**: Safe memory reclamation without garbage collection
- **NUMA awareness**: Socket-local memory allocation, cross-socket traffic minimization
- **Performance analysis**: Latency bounds, contention handling, microbenchmark design

## What Makes This Challenging

The candidate must balance correctness (memory safety, ABA prevention) with performance (cache locality, bounded stalls) while considering real hardware constraints (cache line size, NUMA topology). The hazard pointer mechanism adds complexity for safe reclamation without stop-the-world pauses.
